newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU grain crop seen entering crucial phase.
newsitem.headline: EU grain crop seen entering crucial phase.

text.p: The next two weeks could be decisive for the 1997 European Union grain harvest, Coceral, the EU grain trade lobby, said on Friday.

"If there is sunshine, yields could improve by two percent. If it continues to rain, there will be a big feed quality crop," said a Coceral official, speaking after the forecast was presented at a meeting of the EU cereals advisory committee.
The committee brings together members of the European Commission, farmers and grain traders.
The EU barley crop has been damaged in many regions after a prolonged wet spell. Earlier in the year crops were stressed by a long period of dry weather.
June was the wettest month for a century in Britain, where the barley harvest is likely to be delayed by up to three weeks.
In southern Germany, the malting barley crop is suffering from too high protein content.
In Spain, a lack of quality durum wheat was reported.
Coceral forecast the average EU grain yield falling 4.7 percent to 5.28 tonnes per hectare, from 5.54 tonnes per ha in 1996.
Lower yields were expected to outweigh a 2.7 percent area increase to 37.36 milllion hectares, from 36.36 million in 1996.
